Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - skills/presentation/scripts/scaffold.mjs:129 Precondition: the build script selects its tsconfig with `--project=tsconfig.app.json`, or uses `vue-tsc`. Trace: `tscInvocations` only recognises `-p` and `--project` as separate tokens, and only matches tokens equal to `tsc` or ending in `/tsc`. With `tsc --project=tsconfig.app.json && vite build`, the `=` form matches neither check, so `projects` falls back to `['tsconfig.json']`. With `vue-tsc`, no invocation is found at all. `buildTsconfigs` then never reads the tsconfig that actually names the deleted `vite.config.ts`. Failure: `viteBuild` returns true for a zero-config build, so `detectAnchors(...).build` is reported as present. The scaffold keeps the project's build setup, and `tsc` then fails on the missing vite config. The old behaviour of scanning every tsconfig would have flagged this case, so this is a regression for those forms.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - skills/presentation/scripts/scaffold.mjs:63 Precondition: a registry file contains a regex literal with a quote character (for example `/'/`), or a quote or apostrophe in a place the scanner does not parse (such as JSX text). Trace: `blankComments` has no regex-literal or JSX awareness. It treats the quote as the start of a string and scans to the next matching quote, which may be far away. Any real `//` or `/* */` comment in that span is then copied through unblanked, and a commented-out example entry is parsed as a real route. If no closing quote exists, the rest of the file is kept verbatim. Failure: commented examples can be listed as presentations, and `insertRegistryEntry` can choose the wrong array. `verify.mjs` has the same copy and could then visit a non-existent route. The steps are built as kit Step objects with groupKey, Scene and payload. SampleScene is typed with the kit&#39;s SceneProps and composes the kit&#39;s SceneLayer, Appear, Box, Label, SymbolChip, Arrow, Emphasis and Frame, each given a layoutId. Stage mounts the step&#39;s Scene inside the kit&#39;s LayoutGroup/AnimatePresence, keyed by sceneKey(step). The demo reimplements no kit mechanism. The kit supplies no styling, so an unstyled kit has no active-specific visual treatment."},{"line":1227,"text":"- What the code does (inspection only): `scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs` builds a signature from computed color, background, border, opacity, font weight, text decoration, shadow and outline, plus the rendered `width` and `height` taken from `getBoundingClientRect()`. It warns only when the active entry's signature equals the signature of every inactive sibling. The unit test \"accepts a distinct size\" treats any width delta as sufficient. The integration test exercises indistinct progress items and uses an explicitly styled ToC only as a negative control."},{"line":1228,"text":"- Ruling:"},{"line":1229,"text":" - The diagnostic must still warn when the active entry's styling is identical to the inactive entries' and only the rendered size differs because the labels have different lengths."},{"line":1230,"text":" - A viewer cannot tell which entry is current from the fact that the entry's text is longer or shorter. Distinction here means distinction caused by active-specific styling."},{"line":1231,"text":" - A size or shape difference counts only when it comes from styling that differs between active and inactive entries. Examples are padding, min-width, font size, transform or margin set on the active hook, or progress dots widening into a pill (progress items have identical content, so there a rendered-size delta is style-driven)."},{"line":1232,"text":" - The current check can therefore miss the case. In an unstyled ToC, the era labels have different lengths, so `width` differs for every active entry, the signature differs, and the warning is suppressed. That is a false negative against the canonical scenario, and the helper does not comply as implemented for ToC entries."},{"line":1233,"text":" - The \"accepts a distinct size\" unit test and the absence of an unstyled-ToC variant in the integration test are verification gaps that encode the same misreading."},{"line":1234,"text":" - The fix is wholly within the helper: compare style-driven properties, or content-independent size properties, and add a ToC variant with unequal label lengths and no active styling."},{"line":1235,"text":"- Rationale: the spec says \"visually indistinguishable\", and the purpose is to catch chrome where the current step cannot be told apart. Counting intrinsic text width would make the warning disappear for the most common unstyled ToC."},{"line":1236,"text":"- Pending decision from the user: none. A compliant implementation is possible."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-26ef13ab4c47f762 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":2009,"end_line":2014,"lines":[{"line":2009,"text":"- **Modify an existing presentation:** \"Modify\" step 1 (read-only: resolve the app and"},{"line":2010,"text":" identify the presentation), then 2 Resolve the target and scaffold (a no-op when all"},{"line":2011,"text":" three anchors exist), then the rest of \"Modify\", then 4 Self-verify. The user can change the default URL in a single constant."},{"line":1119,"text":""},{"line":1120,"text":"## Does the kit's style neutrality allow any inline styles?"},{"line":1121,"text":"- Requirement: the kit has zero visual defaults, but the canvas and `SceneLayer` need geometry."},{"line":1122,"text":"- Ruling: the kit may set only layout-geometry properties (position, width, height, transform, inset, display, flex or grid placement, overflow, z-index, pointer-events). A contract test enforces this by scanning the kit."},{"line":1123,"text":"- Rationale: this reconciles \"geometry is layout behavior\" with \"zero defaults\"."},{"line":1124,"text":"- Pending decision: none."},{"line":1125,"text":""},{"line":1126,"text":"## Which template files must stay byte-aligned with the canonical kit?"},{"line":1127,"text":"- Requirement: the test plan says \"non-test scene-kit files ... where parity is required\". Root `scripts/verify.mjs` and `scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs` are likewise aligned with their template copies."},{"line":1129,"text":"- Rationale: a strict rule is simple to test, and CLAUDE.md asks for it."},{"line":1130,"text":"- Pending decision: none."},{"line":1131,"text":""},{"line":1132,"text":"## How are the integration and end-to-end tests separated from `npm test`?"},{"line":1133,"text":"- Requirement: the test plan names INT-001, INT-002, E2E-001, and E2E-002 and says they run in the \"automated integration suite\" and the \"browser-backed end-to-end suite\". A monorepo root may already have a Vite build."},{"line":1140,"text":"- Ruling: anchors are evaluated for the resolved target directory. In a monorepo the target is `presentations/`, and that app is self-contained: it gets its own `package.json` and build setup, its own scene kit, and its own index. The monorepo root's files are never modified. If the user is already inside a presentation app, that app is the target, and only its missing anchors are scaffolded."},{"line":1141,"text":"- Rationale: \"self-contained\" cannot be satisfied by borrowing the root's build setup."},{"line":1142,"text":"- Pending decision: none."},{"line":1143,"text":""},{"line":1144,"text":"## Monorepo detection signal"},{"line":1145,"text":"- Requirement: the design leaves the signal set open."},{"line":1146,"text":"- Ruling: any one of a `workspaces` field in `package.json`, a `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, or a `packages/` or `apps/` directory marks a monorepo."},{"line":1147,"text":"- Rationale: this is the union the design lists. The skill still states the target and gets confirmation before writing to a non-empty project."},{"line":1148,"text":"- Pending decision: none."},{"line":1149,"text":""},{"line":1150,"text":"## Exact sample text"},{"line":1151,"text":"- Requirement: titles and captions are \"normative\"."},{"line":1152,"text":"- Ruling: titles and captions are compared as exact strings copied from the spec table, including the ASCII apostrophes, the em dashes, and the trailing punctuation. Browse mode shows the caption text, and present mode shows the title."},{"line":1153,"text":"- Rationale: \"normative\" plus a verification step that checks \"every normative title and caption\" implies exact match."},{"line":1154,"text":"- Pending decision: none."},{"line":1155,"text":""},{"line":1156,"text":"## Verification failure semantics"},{"line":1157,"text":"- Requirement: \"step error\" and \"console or page error\" are listed separately."},{"line":1158,"text":"- Ruling:"},{"line":1159,"text":" - A console error, a page error, or a step index that does not advance after `ArrowRight` all fail verification."},{"line":1160,"text":" - Each failure message names the phase (`build`, `sample`, `render`) and the 0-based step index."},{"line":1161,"text":" - A missing or out-of-order sample fails in the `sample` phase before any browser starts."},{"line":1162,"text":" - The preview process is always killed, including on failure."},{"line":1163,"text":"- Rationale: these are the cases the failure-contract test covers."},{"line":1164,"text":"- Pending decision: none."},{"line":1165,"text":""},{"line":1166,"text":"## Screenshot helper contract"},{"line":1167,"text":"- Requirement: \"predictable project-local artifact directory\", \"standard desktop viewport\", \"configured settle interval\", and warnings that are advisory."},{"line":1168,"text":"- Ruling:"},{"line":1169,"text":" - Invocation is `npm run inspect -- <slug> [--viewport WxH] [--settle ms]`."},{"line":1170,"text":" - Screenshots go to `inspection/<slug>/step-NN.png` (1-based, zero-padded). That directory is gitignored."},{"line":1171,"text":" - The default viewport is 1440×900 and the default settle interval is 800 ms."},{"line":1172,"text":" - Warnings are printed as `WARN step N: …` lines and do not change the exit code. Operational failures (unknown slug, preview not ready) exit non-zero."},{"line":1173,"text":" - An overlap is two visible text or chrome elements whose boxes intersect, unless either sits inside a `data-presentation-allow-overlap` subtree."},{"line":1174,"text":" - Active chrome counts as indistinct when its computed color, background, border, or opacity matches the inactive siblings'."},{"line":1175,"text":" - Attribution counts as unpolished when its font size is below 11 px or its computed styles equal the browser default link style."},{"line":1176,"text":"- Rationale: the spec leaves the thresholds and paths open, and tests need deterministic values."},{"line":1177,"text":"- Pending decision: none."},{"line":1178,"text":""},{"line":1179,"text":"## Skill procedure behaviors are checked by inspecting `SKILL.md`"},{"line":1180,"text":"- Requirement: gathering, confirmation, scoped modification, and similar behaviors are non-deterministic agent behavior."},{"line":1181,"text":"- Ruling: they are checked by inspecting that `SKILL.md` states each rule explicitly and unambiguously. Template-path resolution relative to the skill directory is also checked by running the materialization code from another working directory (INT-001)."},{"line":1182,"text":"- Rationale: an agent following the workflow cannot be run as an automated check here."},{"line":1183,"text":"- Pending decision: none."},{"line":1184,"text":""},{"line":1185,"text":"## Does a retained, already-entered `Appear` wrapper around a continuing entity comply with \"not wrapped in newcomer fade-in behavior\"?"},{"line":1186,"text":"- Requirement: evolving spec, \"Persistent grouped scenes\" / \"Continuing entities are not faded as newcomers\": an entity that continues across grouped steps \"morphs through layout projection without being wrapped in newcomer fade-in behavior\". The same requirement says a new entity \"animates in after the persisting entities have moved\". design.md says `Appear` \"sequences newcomers only after persisting entities settle\". The checklist rows M-28 and M-31 go further and say to \"assert no `Appear` wrapper is added\" for a continuing entity."},{"line":1187,"text":"- What the code does (inspection only):"},{"line":1188,"text":" - `SampleScene.tsx` `renderEntity` wraps every entity in `<Appear key={e.id}>`, and `templates/presentation/Scene.tsx` does the same."},{"line":1189,"text":" - `SceneLayer` hosts the children in `AnimatePresence`."},{"line":1190,"text":" - `Appear` sets `initial={{opacity:0}}`, `animate={{opacity:1}}` and a delayed transition."},{"line":1191,"text":" - The only continuity test, `continuity.test.tsx`, uses a bare `Box` for the continuing entity and an `Appear` only for the newcomer. It does not exercise the sample's pattern."},{"line":1192,"text":"- Ruling:"},{"line":1193,"text":" - The requirement is about behavior. A continuing entity must not be treated as a newcomer: it must not be remounted, must not replay the fade-in or its delay, and must keep its `layoutId` projection."},{"line":1194,"text":" - A keyed `Appear` that was attached when the entity first entered, and that stays the same mounted instance on later grouped navigations, complies. `initial` runs only on mount, and `animate` and `transition` do not re-run when `animate` has not changed. So nothing newcomer-like happens on the continuing transition."},{"line":1195,"text":" - A wrapper that is added on the entity's first step and removed later would change the element tree. That would remount the entity, which is the opposite of what the requirement protects. A retained wrapper is therefore the only way to give an entity a newcomer fade without remounting it."},{"line":1196,"text":" - Sample-specific verification is still needed. `continuity.test.tsx` does not establish this, because it never exercises an `Appear`-wrapped continuing entity. A test is required on the sample's `SampleScene` pattern, or on a fixture that uses the same pattern (a keyed `Appear` around a `layoutId` child). The test is satisfied when, across a grouped step change:"},{"line":1197,"text":" - the wrapper DOM node and the child DOM node are identical before and after;"},{"line":1198,"text":" - the wrapper's opacity never restarts from 0;"},{"line":1199,"text":" - the wrapper's `key` is unchanged;"},{"line":1200,"text":" - no second `data-presentation-appear` node appears for the entity."},{"line":1201,"text":" - The M-28 and M-31 wording \"no `Appear` wrapper for a continuing entity\" is stricter than the spec. It holds for a fixture that introduces the entity without a fade. It is not required of the sample, which introduces every entity as a newcomer. The spec governs, so the sample is not non-compliant on that ground alone, and the checklist wording is not a requirement."},{"line":1202,"text":" - The `Appear` docstring, \"Continuing entities must not be wrapped in it\", is inconsistent with the sample and the template. It should be read as \"must not be re-wrapped or re-faded\", which is a wording issue and not a requirement change."},{"line":1203,"text":"- Rationale: this is the only reading under which a newcomer can fade in and later morph as the same instance, as the specs require together. The gap is evidence, not implementation."},{"line":1204,"text":"- Pending decision from the user: none. A compliant implementation is possible without one. Compliance is not yet demonstrated for the sample pattern until the targeted verification above exists."},{"line":1205,"text":""},{"line":1206,"text":"## Are class/style/data passthrough props required on chrome components, or only stable CSS-targetable hooks?"},{"line":1207,"text":"- Requirement:"},{"line":1208,"text":" - evolving spec, \"Kit primitives expose style hooks\": \"a presentation composes scene kit primitives or chrome ... the rendered markup exposes stable hooks that presentation-owned CSS can target\". Visual choices come from the presentation or host."},{"line":1209,"text":" - evolving spec, \"Coordinate-heavy diagrams are supported\": \"kit primitives expose class/style hooks\"."},{"line":1210,"text":" - design.md, generic node primitives: \"Each accepts stable identity and class/data/style hooks\"."},{"line":1211,"text":" - Chrome requirements name only specific hooks:"},{"line":1212,"text":" - \"stable active-state hook\" for progress and ToC entries;"},{"line":1213,"text":" - \"a stable presentation hook\" for the attribution;"},{"line":1214,"text":" - a host-provided brand for the top-left slot;"},{"line":1215,"text":" - \"overriding attribution options\" for the attribution."},{"line":1216,"text":"- What the code does: `Header`, `Footer`, `Toc` and `Attribution` take only domain props (`step`, `index`, `mode`, `title`, `brand`, `steps`, `onJump`, `href`, `label`). They hard-code layout geometry in inline styles. They carry stable `data-presentation-*` hooks, `aria-current`, and the active-state hook. `nodes.test.tsx` asserts class, style and data passthrough for the eight primitives and only hooks for chrome."},{"line":1217,"text":"- Ruling:"},{"line":1218,"text":" - Approved: stable, CSS-targetable `data-presentation-*` hooks on every chrome piece (including the active-state and attribution hooks). Class, style and data passthrough is required of the primitives: `Box`, `Label`, `Arrow`, `Frame`, `Emphasis`, `SymbolChip`, `Appear` and `SceneLayer`."},{"line":1219,"text":" - Not required: class, style or data props on `Header`, `Footer`, `Toc` and `Attribution`. The spec text and the design name the passthrough only for primitives and ask chrome only for hooks."},{"line":1220,"text":" - Hard-coded inline geometry on chrome is permitted. The style-ownership requirement says default geometry for the canvas and chrome placement is \"layout behavior, not a visual style system\". Colors, fonts, borders and shadows come from presentation CSS targeting the hooks."},{"line":1221,"text":" - Checklist row M-34 (\"Every primitive and chrome piece ... forwards class/style/data customization\") is stricter than the approved definition. The implementation does not fail the approved definition by omitting chrome passthrough, and the row should not be treated as an unmet requirement."},{"line":1222,"text":"- Rationale: design.md lists the passthrough in the paragraph about generic node primitives, and the chrome requirements ask for hooks only. Adding chrome prop passthrough would be an enhancement and not a requirement."},{"line":1223,"text":"- Pending decision from the user: none. The implementation complies."},{"line":1224,"text":""},{"line":1225,"text":"## Does natural, label-dependent width count as a visible active distinction in the inspection helper's \"indistinct active chrome\" check?"},{"line":1226,"text":"- Requirement: verification spec, \"Indistinct active chrome is reported\": when the active progress indicator or active table-of-contents entry \"is visually indistinguishable from inactive controls\", the helper prints an advisory warning identifying the chrome. presentation-skill, \"Active chrome and attribution are styled locally\", says presentation-owned or host-owned CSS must make the active step visibly distinct. The kit supplies no styling, so an unstyled kit has no active-specific visual treatment."},{"line":1227,"text":"- What the code does (inspection only): `scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs` builds a signature from computed color, background, border, opacity, font weight, text decoration, shadow and outline, plus the rendered `width` and `height` taken from `getBoundingClientRect()`. It warns only when the active entry's signature equals the signature of every inactive sibling. The unit test \"accepts a distinct size\" treats any width delta as sufficient. The integration test exercises indistinct progress items and uses an explicitly styled ToC only as a negative control."},{"line":1228,"text":"- Ruling:"},{"line":1229,"text":" - The diagnostic must still warn when the active entry's styling is identical to the inactive entries' and only the rendered size differs because the labels have different lengths."},{"line":1230,"text":" - A viewer cannot tell which entry is current from the fact that the entry's text is longer or shorter. Distinction here means distinction caused by active-specific styling."},{"line":1231,"text":" - A size or shape difference counts only when it comes from styling that differs between active and inactive entries. Examples are padding, min-width, font size, transform or margin set on the active hook, or progress dots widening into a pill (progress items have identical content, so there a rendered-size delta is style-driven)."},{"line":1232,"text":" - The current check can therefore miss the case. In an unstyled ToC, the era labels have different lengths, so `width` differs for every active entry, the signature differs, and the warning is suppressed. That is a false negative against the canonical scenario, and the helper does not comply as implemented for ToC entries."},{"line":1233,"text":" - The \"accepts a distinct size\" unit test and the absence of an unstyled-ToC variant in the integration test are verification gaps that encode the same misreading."},{"line":1234,"text":" - The fix is wholly within the helper: compare style-driven properties, or content-independent size properties, and add a ToC variant with unequal label lengths and no active styling."},{"line":1235,"text":"- Rationale: the spec says \"visually indistinguishable\", and the purpose is to catch chrome where the current step cannot be told apart. Counting intrinsic text width would make the warning disappear for the most common unstyled ToC."},{"line":1236,"text":"- Pending decision from the user: none. A compliant implementation is possible."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-26ef13ab4c47f762 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":1237,"end_line":1336,"lines":[{"line":1237,"text":""},{"line":1238,"text":"## Must ambiguity resolution for a modify request come before scaffold writes?"},{"line":1239,"text":"- Requirement: presentation-skill, \"Modify an existing presentation\" / \"Target unspecified or ambiguous\": when asked to modify a presentation without a clear target, the skill \"lists the existing presentations and asks which to modify before changing anything\". \"Self-bootstrapping scaffold\": \"Before creating or modifying a presentation, the skill SHALL ensure the project provides the infrastructure ... and SHALL scaffold whatever is missing\". \"Non-empty project missing scaffolding\": the skill states the target location and proceeds only after the user confirms."},{"line":1240,"text":"- What the code does: the top-level workflow in `skills/presentation/SKILL.md` puts \"2 Resolve the target and scaffold\" first for modify and says \"Always finish step 2 before creating or modifying anything\". The Modify section later says to list candidates, ask which one, and \"Change nothing until the target is identified\". Step 2 runs `scaffold.mjs scaffold <project-dir> --no-install`, which writes immediately in some partial cases (for example kit and index present, build setup missing) and after the target confirmation in others."},{"line":1241,"text":"- Ruling:"},{"line":1242,"text":" - The two requirements are both satisfiable only in this order: identify the target (list read-only, ask) first, then scaffold missing infrastructure, then edit."},{"line":1243,"text":" - \"Before changing anything\" is literal. Scaffold writes are changes to the project, so they must not happen before the ambiguous target is identified."},{"line":1244,"text":" - The infrastructure requirement is \"before creating or modifying a presentation\", meaning before the edit of that presentation, so it is still met when scaffolding follows target selection."},{"line":1245,"text":" - As written, `SKILL.md` does not comply for ambiguous modify requests. Its top-level \"Always finish step 2 before creating or modifying anything\" rule, combined with a mutating step 2, puts scaffold writes ahead of the list-and-ask. For modify requests whose target is already clear, running step 2 first remains compliant."},{"line":1246,"text":" - If no presentation exists to list (for example, the index is missing), there is nothing to identify. The skill should say so and offer the create flow. It must not scaffold and then edit a presentation that does not exist."},{"line":1247,"text":" - The fix is the ordering and wording in `SKILL.md`. The `list` command is read-only, so no script change is needed."},{"line":1248,"text":"- Rationale: the canonical text fixes the order of the list-and-ask relative to any change, and the infrastructure requirement fixes only that scaffolding precede the edit. This reading honors both."},{"line":1249,"text":"- Pending decision from the user: none. A compliant implementation is possible."},{"line":1250,"text":""},{"line":1251,"text":"## May the overlap detector exempt every ancestor/descendant pair, or must overprinted text between related nodes still warn?"},{"line":1252,"text":"- Requirement: verification spec, \"Suspicious overlap is reported\": \"visible text or presentation chrome overlaps another visible text/chrome element without an explicit allow-overlap marker\" produces an advisory warning identifying the step and elements. \"Intentional overlap can be marked\": a subtree marked as allowing overlap is not reported. design.md, Verification: \"Intentional overlap is exempt only through an explicit allow-overlap marker.\" The \"Visual inspection artifacts\" requirement frames the check as \"suspicious text/chrome collisions\". INT-002 requires the unmarked collision to warn and the explicitly allowed overlap not to."},{"line":1253,"text":"- What the code does (inspection only): `collectSnapshot` in `scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs` collects every element that has its own text node or matches a chrome hook, using the element's full bounding rect. `findOverlaps` skips any pair where one element is an ancestor of the other (line 65) and every pair involving the allow-overlap marker. The unit test \"ignores a parent and its own descendant\" asserts the ancestor exemption. A parent that owns the text \"alpha\" with an absolutely positioned child span containing \"beta\" over the same text produces no warning and carries no marker."},{"line":1254,"text":"- Ruling:"},{"line":1255,"text":" - A blanket ancestor/descendant exemption is not allowed. The definition names the explicit marker as the only exemption, and the requirement is about collisions between visible text or chrome. Related nodes are not excluded from it."},{"line":1256,"text":" - The exemption is also not required in order to avoid false positives. The requirement concerns visible text and chrome, not container boxes. A parent's bounding box containing its child's box is not a collision between visible text, so ordinary nested typography must not warn."},{"line":1257,"text":" - The detector should therefore separate text from container bounds, for example by measuring the client rects of each element's own text nodes (via `Range.getClientRects`) and using the element box only for chrome controls. It should then compare those rects for every pair, related or not."},{"line":1258,"text":" - Under that reading, ancestor/descendant pairs warn only when two distinct pieces of visible text, or a chrome control and unrelated text, intersect. A chrome control and the text inside it are one visible element and do not collide. The marker exemption is unchanged."},{"line":1259,"text":" - The current implementation does not comply for the overprint case. It also under-verifies it, because the unit test and the INT-002 colliding variant use unrelated siblings. The test needs a nested overprint that warns and nested ordinary typography that does not."},{"line":1260,"text":"- Rationale: this satisfies both \"exempt only through an explicit marker\" and the no-false-positive goal, because it changes what is measured and does not exempt related pairs."},{"line":1261,"text":"- Pending decision from the user: none. A compliant implementation is possible."},{"line":1262,"text":""},{"line":1263,"text":"## Acceptance round 0: autonomous interview and repair evidence"},{"line":1264,"text":"- The caller forbids confirmation/clarification and source fixes. Public CLI generation/scaffolding, read-only target listing and scoped scratch edits can be exercised; a real human answering sequential interviews or choosing among ambiguous targets cannot be demonstrated in this pass. No such transcript is claimed."},{"line":1265,"text":"- Existing ruling \"Skill procedure behaviors are checked by inspecting SKILL.md\" permits documentary checking; this is not runtime evidence of another agent following those instructions. Options: accept documentary checking plus actual CLI journeys, or arrange a separately scripted interactive agent/user session. Consequence: AT-001/002 interactive portions remain limitations; no HT obligations are added."},{"line":1266,"text":"- AT-004 may be demonstrated by removing tester-seeded faults in scratch; actual product defects will not be fixed."},{"line":1267,"text":"- Evidence: acceptance-scaffold-transcript.json; acceptance-scoped-modification.json; exploration-log.md."},{"line":1268,"text":"- Pending decision: whether documentary evidence suffices for interactive procedure acceptance."},{"line":1269,"text":""},{"line":1270,"text":"## Acceptance round 0: interrupted scratch build"},{"line":1271,"text":"- First lab setup build exited with signal status 143 after only the npm build/tsc banner. Retained evidence: scratch/acceptance-test/lab/lab-build.log; tool session 73977 returned exit 143. Provenance: npm run build in the scratch lab with copied template and cached dependencies. Cause is unconfirmed; there is no error text attributing it to platform or product. Same-config retry is being retained as scratch/acceptance-test/lab-build-retry.log."},{"line":1272,"text":"- Pending decision: none if retry succeeds; a failed retry remains an impediment."},{"line":1273,"text":""},{"line":1274,"text":"### Round 0 scratch-run clarification"},{"line":1275,"text":"- Correction: interrupted-build banner is at `scratch/acceptance-test/lab-build.log`, not lab/lab-build.log. Same-config retry `scratch/acceptance-test/lab-build-retry.log` completed successfully."},{"line":1276,"text":"- One original full-copy fault run exceeded the tester's 90-second subprocess deadline in the missing-sample build phase. Retained excerpt in `scratch/acceptance-test/faults-progress.log`: `subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '['npm', 'run', 'verify']' timed out after 90 seconds`. Provenance: public npm verify in scratch/fault-missing-sample; no product failure message or external attribution was established. Subsequent disposable bootstrap copies use 300-second deadlines. This is not evidence that the product is broken."},{"line":1277,"text":"- Two harness-only path mistakes failed before reaching product operations (wrong log directory and a duplicated lab/lab path); corrected runs provide the product evidence. Restarting the harness also encountered existing dependency symlinks, corrected by reusing them."},{"line":1278,"text":"- AXI was launched with an explicit scratch profile and scratch TMPDIR. Earlier direct Playwright/public verify/inspect subprocesses inherited the host default temp location (reported by node:os as /tmp) for internal browser profiles. They automatically cleaned up on close, but this did not meet the caller's requested temp isolation. Later fault subprocesses explicitly use the scratch temp directory. Own fixtures, server working directories, build outputs and retained screenshots are in caller scratch/evidence throughout. This procedural limitation cannot be retroactively removed; no claim of full temp isolation is made."},{"line":1279,"text":"- Pending product decision from this entry: none. Interrupted-run causes remain unconfirmed; successful retries supersede them only as behavioral evidence."},{"line":1280,"text":""},{"line":1281,"text":"## Acceptance round 0: supported Node versions"},{"line":1282,"text":"- Implementation session report identifies direct TypeScript metadata imports through Node type stripping (22.18+). The approved scope supplies no supported Node range, and package.json has no engines field. This pass used Node 24.16.0."},{"line":1283,"text":"- Options: document/enforce Node 22.18+; or support older Node by transforming metadata. Consequence: verify may fail on older runtimes despite a successful Vite build. No older-runtime support failure is claimed here."},{"line":1284,"text":"- Evidence: acceptance-verification-faults.json and scripts/verify.mjs loadSample; implementation _session-report_.out."},{"line":1285,"text":"- Pending decision: supported Node range."},{"line":1286,"text":""},{"line":1287,"text":"## Acceptance round 0: styled reference sample in bootstrap"},{"line":1288,"text":"- The bootstrap includes the mandatory reference sample and its presentation-owned CSS. Fresh unstyled presentations use browser defaults; no default kit palette/font/border was observed. The implementation session report flags whether including a styled sample conflicts with \"zero presentation styling defaults\"."},{"line":1289,"text":"- Options: accept the sample as presentation-owned example styling; or distribute an unstyled example/change sample verification policy. Consequence: every bootstrapped app currently carries the reference sample and verification requires it."},{"line":1290,"text":"- Evidence: acceptance-motion-client.json unstyled computed values; acceptance-scaffold-transcript.json; bootstrap sample/talk.css."},{"line":1291,"text":"- Pending decision: whether a styled example counts as a scaffold styling default. This pass does not make that scope decision."},{"line":1292,"text":""},{"line":1293,"text":"## Acceptance round 0: triage of AF-001 to AF-004"},{"line":1294,"text":"- Question: how are the four findings from the first acceptance round resolved, and does any need a user decision?"},{"line":1295,"text":"- Requirement: evolving spec \"Browse mode is reading-focused\", \"Direct jump\" and the skill's \"Visual composition is inspected\" (AF-001); presentation-skill \"Self-bootstrapping scaffold\" detection by contract, not byte-identical files (AF-002, AF-004); verification spec \"Suspicious overlap is reported\" (AF-003)."},{"line":1296,"text":"- Ruling: all four are implementation defects that contradict the approved definition, so all four are fixed and none is dismissed."},{"line":1297,"text":" - AF-001 (narrow browse layout clips Next and Present). The cause was a CSS specificity bug in the sample's `talk.css`: `[data-presentation-footer] button` padding (6px 12px) outranked the progress dots' `padding: 0`, so each dot was at least 26px wide and the row overflowed even before the phone width. The dots are now selected as `[data-presentation-footer] [data-presentation-progress-item]`, and a `max-width: 480px` block compacts the footer padding, button padding and gaps and lets the progress group shrink. The kit is untouched, so style neutrality and kit parity hold. The bootstrap copy of `talk.css` was updated to match. The helper reporting no warning for clipped controls is not a defect: clipping is not one of the advisory diagnostics the verification spec defines (\"Visual inspection artifacts\"), so no new diagnostic was added."},{"line":1298,"text":" - AF-002 (a working zero-config Vite app is re-scaffolded). Build detection no longer requires a `vite.config.*` file. A project with the `build` script running `vite`, the vite/react/typescript dependencies, and no tsconfig that still points at a missing vite config counts as the build anchor. A tsconfig that includes a vite config that does not exist still reports the build as missing, because `tsc -b` would fail."},{"line":1299,"text":" - AF-003 (inspector false positives). Text inside an ancestor with zero opacity is now treated as invisible (opacity is multiplied up the ancestor chain). A textless chrome control and the text it contains are treated as one element, consistent with the earlier overlap ruling. Unrelated text overlapping a control, and a nested child overprinting its parent's text, still warn."},{"line":1300,"text":" - AF-004 (quoted registry keys hide presentations). Registry detection, listing, duplicate-slug checking, array insertion, and the `slug` parsing in `verify.mjs` (also used by `inspect-presentation.mjs`) accept quoted or unquoted `slug`, `title`, and `load` keys."},{"line":1301,"text":"- Regression coverage added:"},{"line":1302,"text":" - unit: `talkCss.test.ts` (dot padding and the 480px block), `scaffold.test.ts` (zero-config build anchor, quoted registry), `verify.test.ts` (quoted slugs), `inspect.test.ts` (control and own-label exemption);"},{"line":1303,"text":" - integration, written but not run in this step: `tests/integration/narrow.int.test.ts` (every footer control inside a 390px viewport on every step) and hidden-text and own-label guards in the INT-002 fixture (`tests/integration/inspect.int.test.ts`)."},{"line":1304,"text":" - Unit results are in `evidence/acceptance-fix-unit-1.log`, `evidence/acceptance-fix-unit-2.log`, and `evidence/acceptance-fix-lint-tsc.log` (lint and typecheck clean)."},{"line":1305,"text":"- Rationale: each finding contradicts a requirement or is something an ordinary user would call broken, and each has a fix that stays inside the approved behavior, scope and design."},{"line":1306,"text":"- Pending decision from the user: none."},{"line":1307,"text":""},{"line":1308,"text":"## Acceptance round 1: retest and diff exploration"},{"line":1309,"text":"- Base b3faa27356d8e2e3c46adfb97afdf70f1a3ce78e resolves. Current tested revision e31a0ae5e42b40ab2ed8bd3a5935ce98a77b210a. No repeated first-pass coverage floor."},{"line":1310,"text":"- Four changed seams budgeted and explored after reproducing the four original findings. Working-build detection still misclassifies an app with an unused tsconfig referencing the absent Vite config (AF-005); a quoted-key documentation example becomes a phantom registered route (AF-006). These are clear product failures, not scope ambiguity or external limitations."},{"line":1311,"text":"- Original AF-001..004 reproduce correctly after the fixes; exact current evidence is in round1-axi.json and round1-cli-journeys.json."},{"line":1312,"text":"- All round1 own temporary files, clone/build directories, browser profiles, redirected OS browser temp and server working directories use scratch/acceptance-test/round1. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[],"verification-tooling":[{"id":"verification-step-error-fails","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"The contradiction holds. The review guidance says to fail when the check turns an absent or non-numeric hook into a number that still passes its comparison, and it names the case directly: &quot;Number(null) === 0 on the first step&quot;. In scripts/verify.mjs, checkRoute defines `indexNow = async () =&gt; Number(await chrome.getAttribute(&#39;data-step-index&#39;))`. On the first loop pass it checks `(await indexNow()) !== i` with i = 0. A missing index (null) or an empty string becomes 0, so that check passes and the step counts as valid. This is exactly the comparison the guidance tells reviewers to cite. The pass verdict admits the coercion but argues that the later strict string check in waitForFunction catches it. That check only runs after an ArrowRight. When count === 1, the loop hits `if (i === count - 1) break` first, so a missing index is never caught and verification passes. The guidance names this first-step coercion as a failure condition, so the backstop on longer presentations does not save the verdict. FakePage in tests/unit/verify.test.ts always returns String(this.index), so no test covers an absent or non-numeric index. The step-count handling is fine, since !(count &gt; 0) rejects Number(null) = 0, but the index-hook coercion alone fails this criterion.","evidence":["scripts/verify.mjs: `const indexNow = async () =&gt; Number(await chrome.getAttribute(&#39;data-step-index&#39;))` followed in the loop by `if ((await indexNow()) !== i) throw new VerifyError(&#39;re…","scripts/verify.mjs: `if (i === count - 1) break` comes before the ArrowRight and the waitForFunction strict check `getAttribute(&#39;data-step-index&#39;) === String(n)`. The index hook is never absent or non-numeric in any test.","The guidance for verification-step-error-fails says to fail on this pattern and gives the example &quot;Number(null) === 0 on the first step&quot;."],"citations":["scripts/verify.mjs","tests/unit/verify.test.ts"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":0,"sample":1}],"engineering-quality":[],"testing-evidence":[],"assumption-handling":[]}
